stories.headline: Trump bans CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from White House press access
stories.body:
President Donald Trump banned CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House on Friday. He posted on Truth Social that the outlets report fake news. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that banned outlets purposely write negative news. He said they do this to try to diminish Republicans. Trump said he does not want them in his office. He added that he wants the ban to go as far as possible. Trump also said he intends to sue all three outlets.

The banned organizations and rights groups quickly responded to the decision. CNN called the ban an illegal assault on constitutionally-protected press freedoms. Politico said it will continue to report fairly on the White House. It added that it will defend its First Amendment rights. Bruce Brown of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press called the move flatly unconstitutional. Jameel Jaffer of the Knight First Amendment Institute said excluding journalists based on viewpoint is unconstitutional. Amnesty International accused the administration of trying to stifle scrutiny. Reporters Without Borders said it is exploring legal avenues to respond.

claims.text: US President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social on Friday that he is immediately banning CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House.
Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are banned from the White House due to their constant reporting of 'FAKE NEWS'.
Donald Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that banned outlets 'purposely write negative news' to try to diminish Republicans.
Regarding his White House press ban, Donald Trump stated: 'I don't want them in my office. I don't want them here. I would say the ban would go as far as you can.'
US President Donald Trump stated he intends to sue CNN, Politico, and MS Now.
CNN called Donald Trump's White House ban an 'illegal assault' on fundamental, constitutionally-protected press freedoms.
Politico released a statement saying it 'will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones' and will vigorously defend its First Amendment rights.
Bruce Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, called President Trump's media ban 'flatly unconstitutional' and 'textbook viewpoint discrimination.'

Jameel Jaffer, executive director of the Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University, stated that the press pool is a 'public forum' under the First Amendment and excluding journalists based on viewpoint is unconstitutional.
Amnesty International posted on social media accusing the Trump administration of trying to 'stifle scrutiny and evade accountability' by punishing journalists.
Reporters Without Borders stated it is appalled by Donald Trump's threat to ban news outlets and is exploring legal avenues to respond.

stories.headline: US and Denmark reach security agreement regarding Greenland
stories.body:
The United States, Denmark, and Greenland agreed on Friday to sign a new Arctic security pact. The three leaders announced they expect to sign the deal next week at the United Nations General Assembly. Chairman of the Greenland Government Jens-Frederik Nielsen confirmed the upcoming agreement. US President Donald Trump posted about the deal on Truth Social. Trump said the agreement comes at no cost to the United States. He called the security pact an "Infinite Life" agreement with no end date.

Trump posted that plans will start immediately to build a large military presence in parts of Greenland. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the agreement a historic deal. Rubio said it is a huge win for the United States and the American people. An anonymous US State Department official shared details about the terms. The official said the deal explicitly guarantees complete ability for the US to defend the American continent. This includes permanent military access across Greenland. It also grants permanent basing rights and overflight rights.

The US official said the agreement blocks other world powers. The official said it guarantees China and Russia cannot set up military bases in Greenland. The official added that neither country can send troops to Greenland. Currently, the United States maintains a military installation at Pituffik Space Base in Greenland. That facility operates under existing defense arrangements with Denmark.

Denmark Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen spoke about the value of the pact. Frederiksen said the deal strengthens common security in the Arctic and North Atlantic area. She noted that the deal recognizes the sovereignty of the Kingdom. She added that it respects Greenlandic self-determination.

Donald Trump stated on Truth Social that the Greenland security agreement comes at 'no cost to the United States'.

Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that plans will begin immediately to develop a large military presence in appropriate parts of Greenland.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the agreement a 'historic deal' and a 'huge win for the United States and the American people'.

An anonymous US State Department official stated the Greenland agreement explicitly guarantees the US complete ability to secure and defend the American continent, including permanent access, basing, and overflight rights.
A US State Department official stated the Greenland agreement guarantees that China and Russia cannot set up bases or send troops to Greenland.
The United States currently maintains a military installation at Pituffik Space Base in Greenland under existing defense arrangements with Denmark.

Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen stated the security deal 'strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area' while recognizing the sovereignty of the Kingdom and Greenlandic self-determination.

stories.headline: Suicide bombing and shooting at Pakistan mosque kill at least 21
stories.body:
A suicide bomber and gunmen attacked a mosque near police offices in Pakistan's Kohat district. The vehicle bomb explosion and shooting killed at least 21 people. The attack also injured 80 other people. Fifteen police officers were among those killed in the mosque attack. A four-year-old child was also killed in the bombing. Police killed six armed gunmen and one suicide bomber during the compound attack.

Police in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa suggested a faction of Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan carried out the attack. UN Secretary-General António Guterres strongly condemned the bombing. Guterres said that attacks targeting places of worship are unacceptable.

The attack comes during broader security clashes across Pakistan. A roadside bomb in Hangu district killed six soldiers on Thursday. Pakistani troops killed 10 suspected Taliban militants during raids on Thursday. Security forces also killed seven militants in Balochistan province. Earlier in February, a suicide bombing at an Islamabad mosque killed at least 31 people. Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. They discussed rising tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

Pakistani security forces killed seven militants during two separate operations in Balochistan province.
In February, a suicide bombing at the Khadija Tul Kubra Mosque in Islamabad killed at least 31 people.
Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Lt. Gen. Asim Malik to discuss Afghanistan-Pakistan tensions.

stories.headline: Protests erupt in Nigeria after 37 suspected illegal miners die in custody
stories.body:
Thirty-seven suspected illegal gold miners died in custody in Minna, Nigeria. The men were held in a cell run by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps. An intelligence report showed that overcrowding and poor ventilation likely caused the deaths. The agency initially claimed a diphtheria outbreak might be responsible. It later said the cause of death was unconfirmed. The detainees were buried on Thursday without forensic examinations.

The deaths triggered angry street protests in Minna. Security forces fired tear gas and opened fire on demonstrators. Niger State Governor Umar Bago declared three days of mourning. He imposed a 24-hour curfew following violent attacks on government buildings. Governor Bago also postponed the start of election campaigning.

Nigeria Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo ordered an investigation. He immediately suspended Niger state agency commandant Suberu Siyaka Aniviye. Agency spokesperson Babawale Afolabi said over 50 people were arrested in raids before the deaths.

The NSCDC initially claimed the detainees may have died due to a diphtheria outbreak before later stating the cause of death was unconfirmed.

stories.headline: Bank of Japan raises interest rate to 1.25 percent
stories.body:
The Bank of Japan raised its target interest rate to 1.25 percent on Friday. Policy makers voted 7-2 to increase the rate by 25 basis points. The move brings borrowing costs in Japan to their highest level since 1995. Following the announcement, the Japanese yen fell against the US dollar.

Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda discussed future policy after the decision. Ueda said he would not rule out back-to-back interest rate hikes. He noted that future decisions depend on how price conditions develop. Inflation in Japan stood at 1.9 percent in August.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned currency traders not to bet against the yen. Bessent said he had insight into Japanese policy actions. In late July, the US Treasury sold at least $10 billion in euros to buy yen. That intervention aimed to support the Japanese currency. The Bank of England voted to keep UK interest rates unchanged at 3.75 percent.

stories.headline: Mamata Banerjee petitions Supreme Court after Election Commission freezes TMC symbol
stories.body:
Former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee challenged an Election Commission ruling in the Supreme Court. Her Trinamool Congress faction filed the petition on September 18, 2026. The filing follows an interim order issued by the Election Commission of India on September 17. That order froze the All India Trinamool Congress name and symbol. The decision applies to upcoming West Bengal Assembly byelections in Nandigram and Rejinagar.

The Election Commission gave new names and symbols to both competing party factions. Mamata Banerjee's group received the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress'. Her faction was given a 'football player' symbol. A rival faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee received the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress'. The commission allotted an 'envelope' symbol to Ritabrata Banerjee's group. Both factions are recognized as political parties in West Bengal, Meghalaya, and Tripura.

Mamata Banerjee described losing her party's original name and symbol as a black day in democratic history. She originally founded the All India Trinamool Congress in 1998. She created the party after splitting from the Indian National Congress. She had personally hand-drew the original 'Jora Ghas Phool' symbol. In her court filing, her faction highlighted long delays in disqualification proceedings. Those proceedings against 10 rebel legislators remain pending before the West Bengal Assembly Speaker.

The legal battle follows severe internal party rebellions. Nearly 60 out of 80 Trinamool Congress state lawmakers rebelled after May elections. In June 2026, 20 out of 28 party members in the Lok Sabha merged with another party. They joined the Tripura-based Nationalist Citizens Party of India.

Following the symbol ruling, political plans for upcoming elections shifted. Sanchita Pradhan Dey was initially chosen as candidate for Mamata Banerjee's faction in Nandigram. However, Dey withdrew her nomination. Mamata Banerjee then announced her faction would not contest the Nandigram seat. Instead, her group backed Congress candidate Milan Pradhan. On September 18, 2026, police arrested Pradhan in connection with a 2007 murder case.

stories.headline: US President Donald Trump signs Russia sanctions law targeting energy importers
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump signed a new sanctions bill into law on Friday. The legislation is called the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, who named the bill, died in July 2026. The US Senate passed the bill 86-11 in August. The House of Representatives later approved it in a 262-159 vote.

The law gives the US president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent. These tariffs apply to imports from the five largest buyers of Russian oil or natural gas. The targets include India and China. Countries importing under 15 percent of Russia's natural gas exports may get exemptions. To qualify, they must take significant steps to reduce imports.

India's Ministry of External Affairs issued a warning about the new law. It said the sanctions could hurt India-US bilateral relations. The ministry added that the law could impact global energy markets. The bill also extends the Iran Sanctions Act for five more years.

stories.headline: India rejects Pakistan's account of naval warship collision in Arabian Sea
stories.body:
India has rejected Pakistan's allegations regarding a collision between two warships in the Arabian Sea. The incident occurred on September 15, 2026, between Indian warship INS Kolkata and Pakistani vessel PNS Hunain. India summoned Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires Saad Warraich to lodge a protest. Foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said PNS Hunain performed a dangerous overtaking manoeuvre. He said this violated a 1991 bilateral agreement requiring warships to stay three nautical miles apart.

INS Kolkata sustained no major damage and remained at sea. PNS Hunain was observed returning to harbour after sustaining damage. Pakistan gave a conflicting account of the collision. Pakistan summoned Indian Charge d'Affaires Satyanjal Pandey. It alleged that aggressive manoeuvres by the Indian warship inside Pakistan's economic zone caused the crash.

The last recorded collision between the two navies happened in 2011. In that incident, INS Godavari was marginally damaged by PNS Babur during anti-piracy operations.

Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that PNS Hunain carried out a dangerous overtaking manoeuvre violating Article 10 of the 1991 bilateral agreement requiring warships to maintain a 3-nautical-mile distance.
INS Kolkata sustained no major damage and remained deployed at sea following the collision, while PNS Hunain was observed returning to harbour after sustaining damage.
